source_receipts.location: Abstract: contrasting benthic and hyporheic functional responses to light availability and C:N:P ratios.
source_receipts.finding: The published claim is specifically about different functional responses across the two biofilm compartments under experimental light and nutrient conditions.

source_receipts.location: Data.csv header and Treatments.csv: flume, depth, day, parameter, value; 24 assigned treatment rows.
source_receipts.finding: The official raw data identify 24 flumes assigned to the four light-by-C:N:P treatments and retain both benthic and hyporheic observations.
The published workflow iterates over depth and date, then runs compartment-specific treatment analyses rather than showing a direct depth-by-treatment contrast model.

mapped_roles.system: Experimental stream flumes containing benthic and hyporheic biofilm compartments.
mapped_roles.unit: Flume, with paired compartment measurements and day-7/day-14 observation blocks.
mapped_roles.measurement: Biofilm functional and structural parameters recorded by flume, depth, date, parameter, value, and unit.
mapped_roles.published_baseline: The supplied R Markdown analyses treatment effects separately by compartment and date using PERMANOVA-based workflows.
mapped_roles.published_inference: The paper infers that light and C:N:P conditions have contrasting functional effects in benthic versus hyporheic biofilms.
mapped_roles.claim_boundary: The question concerns support for this experimental compartment contrast, not a universal ecological mechanism or a claim about all streams.

proposed_question: When the two compartments are compared directly at the flume level, does a predeclared depth-by-light-by-C:N:P contrast support the paper's stated contrast after holding out flumes?
fragility: Separate significant or non-significant compartment analyses do not themselves establish that the treatment response differs between compartments.
alternative_explanation: The apparent contrast may result from different scale, variance, missingness, or precision by compartment and day, rather than a direct treatment-by-compartment interaction.
independent_check: Predeclare a flume-level direct contrast for a fixed, documented outcome set; train model choices on a subset of flumes, then assess the signed depth-by-light-by-C:N:P contrast on held-out flumes while retaining the original separate-analysis result for comparison.

outcomes.positive: A stable held-out direct interaction with the predeclared direction supports the narrow published compartment-contrast claim.
outcomes.null: An imprecise or near-zero held-out interaction means the available data do not establish the contrast beyond separate analyses.
outcomes.contrary: A reversed or unstable held-out interaction would challenge the stated contrast and require domain/statistical review before any biological reinterpretation.

material_mismatch: The experimental flumes provide paired, manipulated compartment measurements, whereas the paper's ecological interpretation concerns stream biofilms; the proposed result would validate only the experimental contrast.
plain_language_verdict: INTERVIEW-READY CANDIDATE — this packet makes one bounded, reproducible question: whether the claimed contrast is directly supported when the paired compartments and flume assignment are modelled together. It is not a research target yet, has no cross-domain implication, and cannot enter System 2 until an exactly-three candidate trio passes the first-interview gates.
next_permitted_action: Retain this packet without promotion. Build two contrasting packets under the same contract, then run the three-target first-interview gauntlet exactly once.
